A1.justification: Both readable, complete 24-page PDFs describe the same SQUiD research, including Appendices A–G. Their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original schema-generation, database-construction, tuple-quality and ablation experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D, with numerical results in Tables 3–8.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical experiments and results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix G retain the same four-stage pipeline, triplet processing, tuple ensembling, tool-use prompts and programmatic SQL materialization. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Text2R using the same six BIRD domains and three Kaggle domains, with the same difficulty categories. Section 4 and Appendix B introduce no additional datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The zero-shot direct-SQL baseline and Direct/CoT schema comparisons are unchanged. Figure 3 also retains the same illustrative comparisons with T3, STRUCTSUM and EVAPORATE.

E3.justification: The five model configurations, dataset construction, sample counts, evaluation metrics and thresholds, schema-format filtering and join-based evaluation remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B–D.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Tables 6 and 8 retain the same analyses of text-only, symbolic-triplet, schema-aligned-triplet and ensemble inputs. No ablations, robustness tests or case studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point-estimate summaries without seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 3–8 retain their numerical entries, improvement factors and associated findings, including the appendix results. For example, DeepSeek-CoT average entity coverage remains 78.8% in Table 3.

T1.justification: The Text2R formulation in Section 2, database definitions in Appendix A and metric definitions and equations in Appendix C are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The claims concerning the Text2R task, four-stage neurosymbolic framework, benchmark and metrics, and superiority over direct prompting retain the same scope in the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: Explanations involving complementary triplet sources, context length and model failures remain unchanged. The limitations concerning central-table schemas, missing few-shot/fine-tuned comparisons and limited real-world evaluation are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract statement that code and datasets are publicly available, together with a repository link absent from v1. Implementation details and prompts are unchanged; Appendix F.1 still retains the earlier promise of a future generated-dataset release.

R1.justification: The bibliography revises the authors, subtitle and publication information for gTBLS (Sundar et al., 2024). The same named system remains in the unchanged related-work discussion, making this a bibliographic update rather than changed research coverage or positioning.

P1.justification: Edits add the artifact-availability sentence, specify 'Ann Arbor' in the affiliation and revise the gTBLS bibliography entry. Section organization and the scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page author block changes from one line to two, and text reflows with small shifts in placement. Figures 1–20 and Tables 1–8 retain the same content and basic designs.

improvement.justification: The new repository address and explicit availability statement provide concrete artifact-access information missing from v1, improving reproducibility documentation. The gain is limited: scientific methods and evidence are unchanged, and Appendix F.1 still retains inconsistent future-release wording.
